A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LPW research, with matching authors, problem formulation and core workflow. Their text, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: V1 reports original LPW and SLPW benchmark experiments, ablations, parameter studies and manual analyses of generated plans and programs.

after.justification: V2 retains original LPW experiments and reports additional MapCoder comparisons, LiveCode evaluations and token-budget analyses.

M1.justification: V1's separate SLPW method, including multiple-plan sampling, UCB-based allocation and competitive program refinement, disappears along with Section 4 and Appendix Algorithms 1–2. The core LPW procedure remains materially unchanged; the expanded prompt documentation does not establish a procedural modification.

E1.justification: V2 adds evaluation on 140 LiveCode problems dated November 2023–September 2024, described as postdating GPT-4o's training cutoff. This introduces an explicit contamination-oriented generalization scenario. HumanEval, MBPP, their ET variants, APPS and CodeContests remain covered.

E2.justification: V2 adds evaluated MapCoder comparisons in Tables 1 and 3 and the HumanEval difficulty and failure analyses. It also introduces Repeated Sampling in token-budget comparisons on APPS, CodeContests and LiveCode. SLPW disappears from the corresponding comparisons.

E3.justification: V2 introduces Repeated Sampling capped by LPW's token consumption, an accuracy-per-token metric, MapCoder's three-plan/four-refinement configuration, and a separate 20-iteration LPW experiment. SLPW's sampling configurations are removed. Retained experiments preserve their stated benchmark splits, backbone sizes, two-shot prompting and default 12-iteration limits.

E4.justification: V2 replaces the SLPW sampling-parameter study with a 20-iteration LPW study, expands v1's APPS cost analysis into broader cost and budget-response analyses, and adds LiveCode difficulty and hidden-test failure analyses. SLPW ablations and diagnostic results disappear. The LPW-V ablation moves from v1 Appendix A.3 into v2 Table 4; it is not new.

E5.justification: V1 reports point estimates without repeated-run uncertainty. V2 first reports standard deviations calculated from three runs, adds them to the main result tables, and adds uncertainty bands to Figure 4. This establishes a substantial reporting change, but does not establish an increase in the number of runs performed.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes GPT-4o LPW accuracy from 97.0% to 98.2% on HumanEval and from 84.1% to 84.8% on HumanEval-ET, without documenting a procedural explanation. V2 adds LiveCode, MapCoder, Repeated Sampling and extended-iteration results while removing SLPW results. Most retained LPW scores and ablation values remain unchanged. The new LiveCode difficulty breakdown in Figure 12 does not reproduce Table 2's overall scores.

T1.justification: V2 Section 5 explicitly defines an accuracy-cost ratio as Pass@1 accuracy divided by total tokens; v1 only compares accuracy and token consumption separately. The mathematical problem formulation and LPW verification conditions remain unchanged, and neither version presents theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: V2 removes SLPW as an independent contribution and drops the central claim that combining sampling with debugging further improves LPW. State-of-the-art performance claims are recast around LPW alone, with LiveCode added to their scope. Plan verification remains the central innovation.

C2.justification: V2 develops a task-dependent cost interpretation: LDB is more economical on HumanEval/MBPP, while LPW's overhead is argued to be worthwhile on harder benchmarks. It adds interpretations of LiveCode generalization and MapCoder failures. V1's explanations concerning SLPW's sampling benefits, oversampling failures and reuse of UCB rewards disappear. The new Limitations section largely consolidates previously discussed reasoning and representation concerns.

D1.justification: V2 adds eight stage-specific prompt listings with instructions, output delimiters and one demonstration each, substantially extending v1's illustrated fragments. It directs readers to released code for complete prompts, but supplies no repository link. V1's explicit temperature settings disappear with the SLPW appendix; this is a documentation loss, not evidence of changed temperatures.

R1.justification: V2 adds MapCoder (Islam et al., 2024) and LiveCodeBench (Jain et al., 2024), removes UCB and Waterfall/Scrum references and several sampling-related citations, and sharpens its critique of unverified multi-agent plans and tests. The broader synthesis, prompting and code-refinement positioning remains.

P1.justification: The introduction and conclusion are substantially rewritten around LPW alone. Related work moves from the main text to Appendix A, the sampling section disappears, cost-performance analysis becomes a dedicated section, and the appendices are reorganized into more specific subsections. Much of the core workflow explanation is retained.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column layout and extensively reorganizes displays. V1 Figure 4 is split between the main text and appendix; plots gain revised legends and uncertainty displays; cost figures expand; feature tables are merged; and prompt listings are added. Existing workflow diagrams and case studies are largely retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: The token-budget sampling control better addresses whether LPW benefits merely from additional computation, while MapCoder comparisons, three-run uncertainty and detailed prompts improve scrutiny of the retained method. Removing SLPW narrows the contribution. These gains are limited by unresolved reporting discrepancies: v2 Figure 12's LPW LiveCode subgroup scores aggregate to about 57.9%, whereas Table 2 reports 59.3%, and Section 5's cost ratios do not align with Figure 5's plotted costs.
